title: Hom out of an extension by zero from a stratum
statement:
In the situation of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-derived], let
$u\colon S\hookrightarrow Z$ be an open immersion, $a=i\circ u\colon S\hookrightarrow X$,
and $a_!=i_*u_!$ (as in [sk-lem-coefficient-heart]). Let $L$ be a finite
locally projective $\Lambda_S$-module with dual
$L^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_S}(L,\Lambda_S)$. Then, naturally in
$K\in\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$,

$$
R\operatorname{Hom}_X(a_!L,K)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_Z(u_!L,R\underline\Gamma_ZK)
\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_S(L,u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK)
\simeq R\Gamma\bigl(S,L^\vee\otimes u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK\bigr).
$$

In particular $\Hom_{\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)}(a_!L,K[q])=H^q(S,L^\vee\otimes u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK)$
for every $q$.

proof.text: The statement defines $a_!:=i_*u_!$ for the given factorization through $Z$, so $a_!L=i_*(u_!L)$. Apply clause (1) of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-derived] with $A=u_!L$; it gives the first natural isomorphism $R\operatorname{Hom}_X(a_!L,K)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_Z(u_!L,R\underline\Gamma_ZK)$. This uses the composite stipulated here, not a comparison between different locally closed factorizations.

Work on the small representatives of the sites fixed in [def-weil-size-convention], with their actual pulled-back commutative ring sheaves. The functor $u_!$ is exact by [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek] and left adjoint to $u^*$ by [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek-adjunction]. The pullback $u^*$ is exact by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Choose a K-injective representative $J^\bullet$ of $R\underline\Gamma_ZK$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Since $u^*$ is right adjoint to the exact functor $u_!$, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] makes $u^*J^\bullet$ K-injective. In degree $q$, the ordinary adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_Z(u_!L,J^q)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_S(L,u^*J^q)$, and its naturality in $J^q$ identifies the differentials. Thus the termwise adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_Z(u_!L,J^\bullet)\cong\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_S(L,u^*J^\bullet)$, and these complexes compute the two derived Hom complexes, proving the second isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives), applied to the exact adjunction in the blueprint second isomorphism

proof.text: For any $\Lambda_S$-module $N$, evaluation $e_N:L^\vee\otimes N\to\mathcal Hom(L,N)$ sends $\varphi\otimes n$ to $(l\mapsto\varphi(l)n)$, using [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For $L=\Lambda_S^m$ it is the coordinate identity on $N^m$. On a covering with $L\oplus L^{\prime}=\Lambda_S^m$, evaluation is block diagonal for this decomposition; its $L$ block is therefore invertible. The local inverses glue because they invert the same map. The dual of the splitting also makes $L^\vee$ a summand of a finite free sheaf. Thus tensoring by $L$ or $L^\vee$ is locally a summand of a finite power of the identity and preserves exact sequences. Here kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; lifts through a sheaf epimorphism in finitely many coordinates exist on a common covering refinement. For any acyclic complex $B$, its tensor with either sheaf is locally a direct summand of $B^m$, hence acyclic. This is exactly K-flatness of $L[0]$ and $L^\vee[0]$ under [def-pc-kflat-complex].

source.place: Tags 08JJ (lemma-dual-perfect-complex), finite-projective evaluation calculation written out here, and 06YN (definition-K-flat)

proof.text: Put $I=u^*J^\bullet$, representing $N=u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK$, and $C=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L[0],I)$. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $C$ represents $R\mathcal Hom_S(L,N)$, and by [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective] it is K-injective, since step 3 proves $L[0]$ K-flat. The definition in [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology] specifies that the unbounded functor $R\Gamma$ is computed on K-injective complexes. Consequently $R\Gamma(S,C)$ is represented by $\Gamma(S,C)$, whose degree-$q$ term is $\operatorname{Hom}_S(L,I^q)$ by [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. This is the global Hom complex computing $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(L,N)$. The maps $e_{I^q}$ of step 3 commute with $d_I$ by their explicit evaluation formula, and give an isomorphism of sheaf complexes $L^\vee\otimes I\cong C$. Hence $R\Gamma(S,L^\vee\otimes N)\cong R\Gamma(S,C)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_S(L,N)$, as required. Exactness of tensor with $L^\vee$ makes the termwise tensor a representative of the ordinary exact tensor functor on $N$, and K-flatness of $L^\vee[0]$ identifies it with derived tensor.

source.place: Tags 0A96 (lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective), 08J7 (section-internal-hom), and 07A5 (section-unbounded, construction RF(F)=F(I)); comparison illustrated by Tag 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U)

proof.text: All comparisons are induced by adjunction or evaluation, so commute with chain maps of K-injective representatives. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], these maps modulo homotopy compute derived morphisms, and quasi-isomorphisms between K-injective representatives are homotopy equivalences. Additive functors and the displayed evaluation maps preserve these homotopies, so the comparisons are natural in $K$ independently of its representative. For a K-injective representative $T$ of $K$, its shift $T[q]$ is K-injective: for every acyclic $B$, $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(X)}(B,T[q])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(X)}(B[-q],T)=0$, since $B[-q]$ is acyclic. A degree-$q$ cocycle in the global Hom complex from $a_!L[0]$ to $T$ is a map $a_!L\to T^q$ killed by $d_T^q$. It defines a chain map $a_!L[0]\to T[q]$; boundaries are maps $d_T^{q-1}h$. A null-homotopy into $T[q]$ has its only possibly nonzero component $s:a_!L\to T^{q-1}$, and yields the map $(-1)^q d_T^{q-1}s$. Setting $h=(-1)^q s$ identifies these maps exactly with the boundaries, by the differential of [def-pur-hom-complex]. Thus the quotient is $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(X)}(a_!L[0],T[q])$, and the same K-injective comparison identifies it with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(a_!L,K[q])$. Taking degree-$q$ cohomology of the three isomorphisms therefore gives the stated $H^q(S,L^\vee\otimes u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK)$.

split_report.summary: Audited the imported three-isomorphism proof against the current basics blueprint. The item has no finished declaration in WeilConjectures. Replaced the under-cited imported steps with five complete steps: closed-support adjunction, exact open extension adjunction and K-injectives, finite-projective evaluation/K-flatness, derived internal Hom and global sections, and shifted-Hom naturality. No new DAG nodes were needed; the parallel smooth-purity node is recorded as same_as. Corrected the earlier attempt’s step 4 by distinguishing sheaf complexes from global-section complexes and citing the full K-injective definition of RΓ rather than inferring an isomorphism from cohomology groups. The a_! identity is the item’s own definition; the coefficient-heart result, whose coefficients and closure factorization are narrower, is not invoked as a theorem. Second reading made shift stability of K-injectives and the null-homotopy sign explicit, strengthened three truncated citation quotes to include their formulas, and independently searched Mathlib for the finite-free sheaf Hom formulation.
split_report.blueprint: First isomorphism: step 1; second isomorphism and K-injective restriction: step 2; finite-projective dual/tensor calculation: step 3; third isomorphism: step 4; naturality and final H^q formula: step 5.
